prompts.task: Plan standard HTTP/runtime traces, metrics and local application logs for ./service without implementing them. Read the actual source and eval/inputs/go-dependency-log-policy-cases.json; keep its fictional scenarios separate from source facts. Write only ./service/.observe/go-dependency-log-plan.md. Choose the newest set of versions that work together within the supplied constraints. Keep the separate fictional locked dependency set unchanged. Show where the chosen APIs would be used in the application. Describe future tests for each logging case and request/shutdown behavior. Add no custom business or GenAI signals. Check the loaded Go guide's setup, exporter helper and caller: say what works, contradicts requirements or needs adapting, citing branches. Use file/terminal reads only; do not edit other files, install anything, run Go/services/models/cloud tools, or use network or UI.

judge_inputs:
Rule: Grade the saved plan against the actual Go source and the separate scenario file. Accept equivalent concise layouts.
Example: A fictional candidate table is planning data, not an installed dependency set.
Evidence: Read service/go.mod, README.md, cmd/kvstore-server/main.go and kvstore/http.go; then service/eval/inputs/go-dependency-log-policy-cases.json, service/.observe/go-dependency-log-plan.md, last_message.md and grade.json.
Insufficient evidence: A plan that merges fictional deployment facts into the actual source baseline.

Rule: Keep this a planning exercise. Do not require real dependency resolution, installation or telemetry.
Example: The fictional table is enough to choose versions now; real go.sum checksums are unavailable.
Evidence: Actual source uses Go 1.22, has no toolchain directive, no OTel modules and no go.sum. Candidate versions, API facts, locks and receivers are fictional.
Insufficient evidence: Claimed real registry, installed API or runtime results, or refusing to choose from the complete supplied table.

Rule: Check the full dependency graph, runtime limits and operator ownership.
Example: Bridge v0.42.0 declares Go 1.22 but requires log modules that need Go 1.23.
Evidence: Use each module's minimum requirements and the operator ceiling. Grade the chosen versions and preserved separate locked graph against rubric-2 and rubric-3.
Insufficient evidence: Checking only direct Go directives, mixing independently newest modules or replacing the frozen graph.

Rule: Assess every logging scenario and the request/shutdown plan separately.
Example: Wrong port, unsupported protocol and constructor failure are three different cases.
Evidence: Check normal logging, explicit opt-out, port mismatch, protocol mismatch, constructor failure, generic headers, both header forms and logs-specific headers alone. Use the detailed assertions in rubric-4 through rubric-6.
Insufficient evidence: One generic isolation statement, or planned checks presented as runtime or receiver proof.

Rule: Verify the plan's assessment of the shipped Go guide against its actual code.
Example: A claimed header-handling branch must exist in the cited helper or caller.
Evidence: Read .agents/skills/references/languages/go.md, including the complete otel.go setup, exporter helper and main() caller. The old otel-instrument/references/languages/go.md is a compatibility pointer. Check endpoint, header, original-sink and log-only-failure promises; accept a source-justified adaptation.
Insufficient evidence: Invented branches, omitted contradictions, or guide code treated as installed-SDK or runtime proof.

Rule: Read all four parts of each criterion together. Examples add no requirements.
Example: Equivalent names and valid observations are accepted unless supplied data fixes an exact value.
Evidence: Apply the stated scope and accept an equivalent plan structure. Source inspection and proposed tests remain planning evidence.
Insufficient evidence: Requiring an example's incidental wording, extra work or runtime execution in this plan-only case.
rubric:
Rule: Plan for the real kvstore service and keep fictional inputs separate.
Example: A proposed otelhttp wrapper belongs at the actual HTTP setup; it is not already installed.
Evidence: Record the actual baseline: module kvstore, Go 1.22, no toolchain directive, no OTel modules and no go.sum. Preserve the cmd/kvstore-server command and flags, HTTP/store APIs and behavior. Map the proposed HTTP wrapper and slog/standard-log bridge to main and the actual request WarnContext and shutdown warnings. Keep all work in the saved plan, without custom business or GenAI spans. Label candidates, APIs, profiles and the separate lock as fictional.
Insufficient evidence: Source/config/test changes, installation, claimed solver/runtime/Studio success, or fictional data presented as actual source facts.

Rule: Choose the newest supplied versions that work together under every constraint.
Example: Reject bridge v0.42.0: its own Go 1.22 directive hides a Go 1.23 transitive requirement.
Evidence: Select otel root, sdk and trace/metric HTTP exporters v1.101.0; log API and sdk/log v0.51.0; log HTTP exporter v0.52.0; otelslog v0.41.0; otelhttp v0.61.0; runtime instrumentation v0.31.0. Explain the minimum-version closure, Go 1.22.8 limit and operator API/SDK ceiling. Reject newer Go 1.23 choices, including that bridge. Keep the separate compatible operator-owned old graph and pipelines, explaining why it remains compatible and must not be upgraded.
Insufficient evidence: Choosing later, independently mixing newest releases, assuming bridge/SDK version numbers must match, changing Go/toolchain/GOTOOLCHAIN, or treating the actual service as already instrumented.

Rule: Plan real preflight first, then apply exactly the checked dependency set in an isolated copy.
Example: A later v0.44.0 bridge release cannot replace the set approved during preflight.
Evidence: Describe future public metadata/API and graph checks with GOTOOLCHAIN=local. Record exact module@release specs for every selected module, or an exact graph/lock. Apply that set in an isolated module copy; inspect go.mod/go.sum, graph, imports and APIs, then run project-native tests. Preserve Go 1.22, the absent toolchain directive and operator constraints. Keep discovery, fictional selection, later application and actual execution distinct.
Insufficient evidence: Floating @latest installs, unresolved placeholders, invented checksums/results, a second mutable lookup during application, or unrelated grpc/Gin/chi/logger bridges.

Rule: Plan one local log pipeline alongside the original logger output.
Example: One successful PUT produces one native LogRecord whose IDs match that request's HTTP span.
Evidence: Use supported HTTP/runtime providers, one otelslog bridge, the same shared go-kvstore Resource across trace, metric and log providers, LoggerProvider, BatchProcessor and HTTP/protobuf exporter at http://127.0.0.1:55318/v1/logs. The normal consumed profile explicitly sets OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER=otlp and the resolved logs protocol. Preserve independent trace/metric routes and the original standard log writer, prefix, flags and slog output through safe nonrecursive fanout. Future acceptance checks one native record per successful PUT: body runtime request completed, WARN, operation put, service go-kvstore and nonzero IDs matching its own HTTP span, plus a span and metric datapoints. Keep records bounded and redacted, without raw keys, values, paths, errors, configuration or credentials.
Insufficient evidence: Configuration or stdout correlation used as receiver proof, duplicate export, an invented file sink, or exporting forbidden data.

Rule: Plan each opt-out and log-only failure without breaking the application, original logger, traces or metrics.
Example: Generic headers skip only added local logs; logs-specific headers alone stay with the approved exporter.
Evidence: For none, add no local provider/bridge and expect zero OTLP logs. Port 55319 is not approved port 55318; grpc cannot use this HTTP-only exporter. A constructor failure skips only added logs and produces a diagnostic without configuration or secret values. Treat generic headers alone and together with logs-specific headers as separate isolation cases: preserve operator values and other signals. With only logs-specific headers, keep the approved path enabled and let the official exporter parse them; do not mask them with empty headers. Keep original warnings and request behavior. Separately cite actual guide setup, exporter-helper and caller branches for endpoints, headers, sinks and log-only failure; explain support, contradictions or necessary kvstore adaptations.
Insufficient evidence: One generic statement for all cases, persisted none as the normal default, silently changed endpoints/protocols, cloud log forwarding, invented guide branches, ignored contradictions, or planned/source checks presented as executed SDK/runtime proof.

Rule: Plan request and shutdown checks at the real log calls, in the correct order.
Example: The shutdown warning is outside a span and must not borrow the earlier request's IDs.
Evidence: Carry request context into the bridge. Plan runtime shutdown completed at WARN without fabricated request IDs. Drain server/store work and emit that final warning while the provider is alive, then perform bounded, once-only shutdown of batches and all owned trace, metric and log providers on normal and signal exits. Normal logging must preserve the sink and deliver the final native record. Opt-out keeps the original final warning with zero OTLP records. Log failures keep the original warning, traces and metrics usable.
Insufficient evidence: Fabricated shutdown correlation, missing final-record/sink checks, or unrun shutdown, sink, wire or cloud checks claimed as completed.
